findings.title: A turn that missed plan-gate before its first outward action is blocked again at every later stop of the same owner turn, after doing exactly what the first block ordered; nothing the assistant can do ends it.
findings.component: lib/hooks/governance-enforce.py:76-92 (plan-gate is looked for only before the first outward call; the turn runs from the owner's last message)
findings.rule_quoted: BLOCK once and force the load. Single retry (stop_hook_active) => loop-safe. // Load the missing governor with the Skill tool now and follow it. The plan comes after the action this time: say so plainly to the owner, then state the goal and what was done.
findings.observed:
ok wb-WD01-stop1 gate: block:F1 rule: block:F1 | stop 1: ungoverned push
ok wb-WD01-stop2 gate: allow rule: allow | stop 2 [retry]: loaded both governors and told the owner, exactly as the block ordered
MISMATCH wb-WD01-stop3 gate: block:F1 rule: allow | stop 3: same owner turn, a background-task notification arrived, one line of reply
ok wb-WD01-stop4 gate: allow rule: allow | stop 4 [retry]: loaded plan-gate again
MISMATCH wb-WD01-stop5 gate: block:F1 rule: allow | stop 5: same owner turn, a GitHub notification arrived, one line of reply
reason printed at stop 3: GOV-ENFORCE: this turn took an outward action (commit, push, PR or merge) without plan-gate (before the first outward action). Load the missing governor with the Skill tool now and follow it. The plan comes after the action this time: say so plainly to the owner, then state the goal and what was done. This applies however short the owner's message was ('continue', 'proceed').
findings.expected: allow at stops 3 and 5: the turn was blocked once and did what the block ordered. The documents nowhere say the same miss is raised again at every later stop. Against this reading: fixture case S3 (lib/hooks/selftest-turn-gates.py:141-143) expects a block on a similar shape (governors loaded after a GitHub notification), so the code is pinned this way and a second reader may class this as ambiguity.
findings.how_it_arises: Ordinary in this owner's sessions. After a push or a PR the session is woken by notifications (the real transcript has 60 GitHub-activity notifications, delivered in 9 notification reads, and 6 task-notification rows) and each wake ends in a new stop with stop_hook_active false. pack/replay-baseline.txt shows, by timestamp, at least 5 of the 17 real owner turns with two or more such stops, and the two real F1 blocks are two consecutive stops of one turn. When the miss is adversarial-verify, loading it cures the turn. When the miss is plan-gate before the first action (fixture cases 1 to 3) nothing can cure it, because the load can no longer come first: every wake then costs a forced continuation, another plan-gate load and another 'the plan came after the action' message, until the owner types again. All row shapes are real (isMeta feedback rows, Skill re-invocations, notification rows).

Answer to angle 7: the two real F1 blocks (2026-10-21T23:26, twice) are right by the stated rule. Both are the audited turn R7 at two consecutive stops; both rest on adversarial-verify missing (probe P1 removes them, P2 keeps them); plan-gate was loaded before the first outward call; no mention-only or errored call is involved (D4, D5, P11). Answer to angle 5: a block prevents nothing. It arrives when the assistant stops, after the commit, push, merge or trigger change, and after its one block the turn may end whether or not anything was loaded (F1-2).
